 By Kasandra Rattle Published on November 16, 2026 2450 Massachusetts Ave. NW — Approximate Washington Street Scene
Google Street View South Korea's Foreign Ministry wants to pursue reconstruction of its aging Washington embassy, a building that has stood since 1954, but the money to do it still has not made it into next year's government budget proposal. The ministry has cited safety issues at the facility, along with constraints on diplomatic work and worries about how the building reflects on the country's image abroad.
 According to Yonhap News Agency , the Foreign Ministry has pushed for reconstruction of the embassy in 2023, 2025 and 2026, each time pointing to safety concerns tied to the aging structure. The Korea Times reports the ministry's reasoning goes beyond just safety, citing limits to performing diplomatic activities in the aging facilities and concerns about the impact on the national image, as described in a report from The Korea Times .
 Cost Estimates Diverge
 Just how much the rebuild would cost depends on which account you read. Yonhap reports the project is estimated to cost 264.6 billion won, or roughly US$198 million. Seoul Economic Daily, meanwhile, puts the figure at about 300 billion won, or around $204 million, a total that the outlet says includes 30 billion won in rent for temporary offices, according to a report from Seoul Economic Daily . The outlets give different estimates, with Seoul Economic Daily including temporary-office costs in its total.
 The Washington Times reported that embassy reconstruction funds must be allocated through the State Property Management Fund rather than accounts tied to the Foreign Ministry itself, as described by the Washington Times .
 Budget Still Undecided
 As of Monday, the ministry's funding request had not yet been included in next year's government budget proposal, Yonhap reported. A National Assembly budget subcommittee was scheduled to discuss on Tuesday and Wednesday, November 17 and 18, whether to include the embassy rebuilding project in next year's general-account budget bill, the same Seoul Economic Daily report noted. Whether lawmakers ultimately agree to fund the project remains to be seen.
 The Washington Times reported that the relevant subcommittee falls under the National Assembly's Foreign Affairs and Unification Committee. The outlet also noted that South Korea's Foreign Ministry has reportedly been interested in rebuilding or renovating the embassy for several past years, a detail consistent with the repeated requests described by Yonhap.
 A Building With a Long History
 South Korea bought the current embassy building in 1990 from another country that had previously used it as its military attaché's office, per Yonhap's reporting. The structure itself dates to 1954, making it 72 years old.
 Korea JoongAng Daily notes that South Korea has rebuilt or newly constructed major diplomatic missions in other countries, including China and Japan, with the Washington embassy standing out as something of an exception, according to Korea JoongAng Daily . That contrast underscores why the ministry has kept pressing the issue year after year even as funding has stalled.
 South Korea has undertaken other historic preservation work on its diplomatic properties in Washington before. The former Korean legation building in the city underwent restoration and repair work from October 2015 through March 2018, reopening to the public in May 2018, according to the Overseas Korean Cultural Heritage Foundation . That project offers a glimpse of how long such efforts can take once they actually move forward, though the embassy rebuild now under discussion is a separate, far larger undertaking whose fate rests with this week's budget talks.
